title: Millennium Whisper is the first on-device AI game on Steam!
author: Dear_Highway_7728
selftext:
**But how did we make this happen?**

**Step one was to start with real performances.**  
Instead of scraping datasets, we worked directly with actors in live sessions, capturing their voices, improvisation, humour, and emotional choices. These performances became the foundation for our characters.

**Step two was to design for local hardware usage.**  
Rather than relying on cloud infrastructure, we built systems lightweight enough to run directly on consumer devices. That meant optimising models, simplifying pipelines, and making sure everything could run without servers or constant connectivity.

**And step three was to build the game around the constraints.**  
If everything runs locally, dialogue systems need to be flexible, characters need memory, and interactions need to feel natural without pre-written branches. Training the AI with real human performances added the much needed personality to make this happen.

  
*No AI was used in the creation of any art assets, music or writing. AI is only used for character interactions and mechanics.*  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/3156240/Millennium\_Whisper/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3156240/Millennium_Whisper/)

comments.author: monsterfurby
comments.body: Love the idea and concept, but I still really wish I could hook it up to OpenRouter or other provider API. My 5070 Ti does local text models just fine, but the few times I tried this before, I kind of wished for a Mantella/Skyrimnet-style customizable multi-model setup for coherence.

replies.author: Dear_Highway_7728
replies.body:
Thanks so much, really glad the concept resonates!  
  
Honestly, OpenRouter/cloud API support isn't something we're planning to add!! The whole Parable Engine is built around on-device AI specifically to avoid cloud dependency, the ongoing costs it creates for players, and the carbon footprint that comes with it. Plugging into external providers would kind of undermine that from the ground up.  
  
The Mantella/Skyrimnet comparison is a fair one though and I totally get the appeal of that! The difference is that our AI is trained on real actor performances rather than general-purpose text models. It's less "LLM with a skin" and more a specialised performance model (which is why mixing and matching providers wouldn't really work the way it does with those tools).

replies.author: eagergm
replies.body: How is the carbon footprint different when using someone else's server vs using your own computer? Is the network transmission really energy intensive? To be fair, I have no idea how the internet works.

replies.author: Dear_Highway_7728
replies.body:
So our entire model training used single 4090 with the whole rig using 500w for two hours, meaning it only used 1kwh per iteration. We did a total of 10 iterations meaning that the entire game's AI development used only 450g of CO2. Which is about the same as roughly 450 ChatGPT queries.   
Basically, if this was being run on Cloud servers, the eco cost (and also financial) would be huge!

replies.author: Zennity
replies.body: Using someone else’s server means you’re probably using a model that is hosted in a data center. Local servers use way less resources and hardware

replies.author: odragora
replies.body:
Data centers have a lot of optimizations, they are a lot more efficient than consumer hardware.

Energy / water consumption of AI is tiny compared to other industries anyway.

replies.author: SadNetworkVictim
replies.body: Data centers spend a *ton* of energy on cooling.

comments.author: xcdesz
comments.body:
This is really great and a step forward in game dev progress, but I still dont get the double standard going with "its ok for text generation but not visual arts, image or voice generation.". Theres so much more we can be doing with this technology but are held back by these loud voices against changes to the system.  

Professionals in the visual arts communities are using these tools, despite the ongoing crusade, and outputs can be made to not imitate existing styles or trademarks or real human voices. replies.author: Dear_Highway_7728
replies.body:
Some people see AI and just instantly get turned off, without even paying attention to what it is (and that they've been using it for years without it being explicitly called that) 


The anger comes from a lot of gen ai scraping data from the internet and taking people's data and work without consent, which I can totally understand! 


With using the Parable Engine to create our game (and potentially for use across industries also) collecting all your own data to feed in leads to the stealing aspect being gone as everything is unique, new work! 


I think the big difference is when it's been used responisbily as a tool as opposed to for... Well.. Just everything?

comments.author: Aware-Source6313
comments.body:
Interesting, you mentioned in comments that each character has their own find-tuned model? I would have expected a single find-tuned "character actor" LLM that was given system prompts, memory, game context, to roleplay as a certain character. Can you explain your choice and if you tried different methods? How many parameters are the models for each character and how much disk space do those weights need? I wonder if you could save space with a general model rather than multiple, or of the fine tuning process makes the specialized voices built into the weights in a way that actually compresses the data as the LLM doesn't need general role playing capabilities with such a specific focus during the fine tuning training.

Cool idea, many have thought of using LLMs for characters, but most try in a pretty tech-illiterate way from what I've seen and just hooked every character up to chatgpt api naively. Managing context effectively typically becomes very important but find-tuned tiny models does seem like a solution to leverage only the useful aspects of LLMs at runtime for a game in a more practical way.

comments.author: lingotionny
comments.body:
Wow that is impressive! On-device with quality is hard to do so kudos to you for making it a reality! I am speaking from experience as someone who is in the on-device AI rabbit-hole too, but with a different focus. I have been part of the team building Lingotion Thespeon which is not an LLM but rather the continuation: a kind of on-device TTS system, but with proper controllable VA performance and emotional delivery in the style of a real actor rather than stale narration. Call it text-to-acting if you will :D

What I find very exciting to see here is that you too seem to have understood that to do AI right in a real-time game setting you really need two things: on-device inference and ethical data sourcing. If you try running on cloud then cloud costs are just going to blow up as the game gathers traction, and using AI trained on scraped data runs the very real risk of running into legal problems like Anthropic did, ending up paying a $1.5 billion settlement for all the books they essentially stole.

Excited to see what you get up to next!
